S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury involving a home battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and provide affected customers and occupants of the directly adjoining homes with an initial safety notice within 24 hours. Near-misses without fire, thermal runaway, or injury must be reported to the regulator quarterly.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The compliance target is that no more than 5% of tested units fail. A model exceeding 5% must promptly submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retest on a regulator-set schedule; exceeding the target alone does not automatically bar market entry or require market withdrawal while the plan is being implemented.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery systems placed on the market from 3 years after adoption must include a remote emergency shut-off capability accessible to the manufacturer and the customer, with safeguards against unauthorized activation. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers must offer a compatible retrofit or replacement pathway and complete required retrofits within 6 years, where technically feasible; customers must be notified of any limitations and interim safety measures.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems placed on the market from 36 months after adoption must include built-in fire suppression designed and tested to contain or mitigate battery fires under the regulator-approved protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers and occupants of directly adjoining homes of material safety risks and provide interim safety guidance. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, notify the regulator and affected customers, and provide a repair, replacement, or refund remedy.

document.section_notes: The final S2 keeps a 5% compliance target but removes any sales stop: models above it only need a corrective-action plan and retesting, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10. S5 sets a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no interim trigger, which forces a remedy on Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). S1 reporting is fast for serious incidents but near-misses without fire or injury are reported only quarterly. Retrofit runs to 6 years (within Northwind's red line) and suppression to 36 months (within Halcyon's red line).
